context.text: This is an open seat: incumbent Tommy Tuberville (R) did not seek re-election. Barry Moore, the sitting U.S. Representative for Alabama's 1st Congressional District, defeated Jared Hudson in the Republican primary runoff on June 16, 2026 to win the Republican nomination. Everett Wess defeated Dakarai Larriett in the Democratic primary runoff on June 16, 2026 to win the Democratic nomination.

candidates.name: Barry Moore
candidates.ballotNote: Won the Republican primary runoff on June 16, 2026, defeating Jared Hudson.
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative for Alabama's 1st Congressional District (since 2025); previously represented Alabama's 2nd District (2021–2025) and the Alabama House of Representatives, District 91 (2010–2018)

summary.text: Barry Moore is the sitting U.S. Representative for Alabama's 1st Congressional District, running for Alabama's open U.S. Senate seat. He previously represented Alabama's 2nd Congressional District from 2021 to 2025 and served in the Alabama House of Representatives from 2010 to 2018. In Congress he sits on the House Agriculture and Judiciary committees.

background.text: Served in the U.S. Army National Guard; earned a bachelor's degree in agricultural science from Auburn University in 1992.
Career experience includes co-owning and co-operating Barry Moore Industries; served in the Alabama House of Representatives, District 91, from 2010 to 2018.

Elected to the U.S. House for Alabama's 2nd District in 2020; after 2023 redistricting merged him into a primary against fellow incumbent Jerry Carl, defeated Carl in the 2024 Republican primary and was elected to represent the renumbered 1st District.

priorities.text: Points to his congressional record, saying he "was rated both the most conservative member in Alabama by CPAC and the state's most effective legislator by the Center for Legislative Excellence."
priorities.quote: was rated both the most conservative member in Alabama by CPAC and the state's most effective legislator by the Center for Legislative Excellence.

priorities.text: On the economy, his campaign website says he "supports small businesses, lower taxes, and American entrepreneurship."
priorities.quote: supports small businesses, lower taxes, and American entrepreneurship.

positions.quote: supports small businesses, lower taxes, and American entrepreneurship.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Agriculture (General Farm Commodities, Risk Management and Credit; Livestock, Dairy and Poultry subcommittees) and the House Committee on the Judiciary (Crime and Federal Government Surveillance; Immigration Integrity, Security, and Enforcement; and Oversight subcommittees) in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).
Served on the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs (Ranking Member, Economic Opportunity Subcommittee) in the 117th Congress (2021-2022) while representing the former 2nd District.

candidates.name: Everett Wess
candidates.ballotNote: Won the Democratic primary runoff on June 16, 2026, defeating Dakarai Larriett.
candidates.currentRole: Midfield Municipal Court Judge, Jefferson County, Alabama (8 years)

summary.text: Everett Wess is a Birmingham attorney and Midfield Municipal Court judge running as the Democratic nominee for Alabama's open U.S. Senate seat. He is Managing Partner of The Wess Law Firm, P.C., has served on the federal Criminal Justice Act panel representing indigent defendants, and is State President of the Alabama New South Coalition, a civic-engagement organization.

background.text: Earned a Juris Doctor from the Birmingham School of Law, an MBA from Alabama A&M University, a bachelor's degree in computer science from Alabama A&M, and an associate degree in music education from Selma University.

Has served as Managing Partner of The Wess Law Firm, P.C. since 2001, practicing primarily in estate planning and criminal defense, and for ten years served on the Federal Criminal Justice Act panel representing indigent defendants in federal court.
Has served for eight years as a Midfield Municipal Court judge in Jefferson County; earlier served as a prosecutor for the City of Midfield and a public defender for the City of Irondale.

priorities.text: Campaign platform centers on "affordable healthcare and economic opportunity," including funding for medical providers and hospitals in rural and underserved areas.
priorities.quote: Protect Alabama Jobs, Healthcare, and Tough fair justice.

priorities.text: Says he is running to advocate for voting rights, equal justice, quality public education, and economic opportunity, and to protect the rights of Alabamians in the courts.
Emphasizes "clean government" and fair courts as part of his campaign for the Senate.

positions.summary: Campaign centers on affordable healthcare, including funding for rural hospitals and medical providers in underserved areas.

candidates.researchNotes: Wess has no Ballotpedia biography beyond his current and past judicial candidacies; background and priorities here are drawn from his campaign website, which does not itemize distinct positions issue-by-issue beyond the general platform quoted above.
